question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation system, including the new config surface, durable continuation state, model-facing continuation tools, and trusted cross-session return policy?
rationale: The implementation is not a narrow bug fix; it defines new core agent behavior and security/session-state semantics that automation cannot choose for maintainers.

options.title: Keep open for owner approval
options.body: Require maintainers to approve the continuation API, cross-session trust posture, upgrade story, and remaining compaction proof before merge.

options.title: Split to smaller core seams
options.body: Ask the author to split storage/tool registration, same-session continuation, cross-session targeting, and compaction into smaller reviewable PRs.

options.title: Decline core feature for now
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers want this experimental lifecycle behavior to live outside core until the product direction is clearer.

recommendation.title: Keep open for owner approval
recommendation.body: Require maintainers to approve the continuation API, cross-session trust posture, upgrade story, and remaining compaction proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows broad recent ownership signals across the affected agent runtime, TaskFlow, system-event, and protocol surfaces.
